titlePlain: Multi-Stage Builds: Separating Build Tools from the
subtitle: Lesson 3 · Docker for Platform Engineers

code:
# Ships the entire Go toolchain in the final image
FROM golang:1.23
WORKDIR /app
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN go build -o server .
CMD ["./server"]
caption: A 10MB binary, wrapped in a build environment it will never call again.

code:
# Stage 1: build, using the full toolchain
FROM golang:1.23 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o server .

# Stage 2: runtime, starting completely fresh
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12
COPY --from=build /app/server /server
ENTRYPOINT ["/server"]
caption: COPY --from=build pulls out one file; everything else from that stage never ships.

steps.label: build stage
steps.sub: npm ci (full) + npm run build — produces dist/

steps.label: runtime stage
steps.sub: npm ci --omit=dev — its own clean, production-only install

steps.label: COPY --from=build
steps.sub: carries forward only the dist/ folder

code:
docker build --target build -t myapp:debug-build-stage .

# default build (no --target) tags the LAST stage in the file
docker build -t myapp .
caption: Useful for inspecting an intermediate stage without shipping it.
